issues.description: Method SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(Meal): The problem statement (UML and explanatory text) specifies that calculateTotalPrice should return a double (use double precision for financial calculations). The reference implementation in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java declares and implements calculateTotalPrice as returning an int. This inconsistency between the specification (double) and the solution implementation (int) can confuse students about the expected return type and the required numeric precision when implementing the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent with the problem statement: change the solution method signature to public static double calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal) and compute the total using double (e.g., double sum = 0.0; sum += (double) ingredient.getPrice(); return sum;). Alternatively, if integer totals are intended, update the problem statement (UML and text) to specify an int return type and remove the mention of double precision. Prefer updating the solution to return double to preserve the stated financial-precision intent.
